d.d: The vertical edge of a sail that is closest to the direction of the wind.
d.x: By easing the halyard, the luff of the sail was made to sag to leeward.

d.d: The act of sailing a ship close to the wind.
The roundest part of a ship's bow.
To shake due to being trimmed improperly.
To bring the ship's head up closer to the wind. (Alternatively luff up)
to let out (a sail) so that it luffs.
